mutableWidening.text: '{{source}}' is seen here as '{{target}}', and `{{slot}}` is mutable. Through the wider type anything that is a '{{targetPart}}' can be written there, and the original, still typed '{{sourcePart}}', then holds it: TypeScript accepts this, and it is a TypeError at runtime. Make the slot read-only in the target type (`readonly T[]`, a `readonly` property, `ReadonlyMap`), so the narrower value is only read through it, or copy the value ([...items], { ...record }).

readonlyMadeWritable.text: '{{source}}' is seen here as '{{target}}', and `{{slot}}` is read-only in the original but writable here. A read-only slot is only ever read, so the '{{sourcePart}}' it holds can be a narrower value, and writing any '{{targetPart}}' through this view leaves the original holding what it never allowed: TypeScript accepts this, and it can be a TypeError at runtime. Keep the slot `readonly` in the target type, or copy the value ({ ...record }).

methodParameterNarrowed.text: '{{source}}' is seen here as '{{target}}', and `{{slot}}` takes only a '{{targetPart}}' where the wider type passes any '{{sourcePart}}': TypeScript compares a method's parameters in both directions, so it accepts this, and a call through the wider type is a TypeError at runtime. Write the member as a property in the wider type (`put: (animal: Animal) => void`), which TypeScript checks one way, or take the wider parameter.
